title: Commutative quotient and transition squares for the finite scalar model
statement:
theorem scalar_finite_squares
    (b : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ leftComplex l E L ι g ≅
      (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ rightComplex l E L ι g)
    (bfin : ∀ n : ℕ,
        (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ finiteLeft l E L ι g n ≅
          (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ finiteRight l E L ι g n)
    (vleft : ∀ n : ℕ,
        (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ leftComplex l E L ι g ⟶
          (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ restrictedLeft l E L ι g n)
    (vright : ∀ n : ℕ,
        (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ rightComplex l E L ι g ⟶
          (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ restrictedRight l E L ι g n)
    (tleft : ∀ n : ℕ,
        (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ restrictedLeft l E L ι g (n + 1) ⟶
          (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ restrictedLeft l E L ι g n)
    (tright : ∀ n : ℕ,
        (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ restrictedRight l E L ι g (n + 1) ⟶
          (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ restrictedRight l E L ι g n)
    (hb : CompletedFormula l E L ι g b)
    (hF : FiniteFormula l E L ι g bfin)
    (hL : LeftQuotientFormula l E L ι g vleft)
    (hR : RightQuotientFormula l E L ι g vright)
    (hTL : LeftTransitionFormula l E L ι g tleft)
    (hTR : RightTransitionFormula l E L ι g tright) :
    QuotientSquare l E L ι g b bfin vleft vright ∧
    TransitionSquare l E L ι g bfin tleft tright

source.place: Tags 03EK and 03EL, Steps 4--6 of the normalized finite model argument.

proof.text: For the quotient square, apply degreewise completed tensor extensionality. Pull the outer coefficient back along the completed coefficient isomorphism, use CompletedFormula and the two quotient formulas, then the finite formula with middle coefficient one. The completed-to-finite coefficient square, followed by the inverse finite comparison, identifies the remaining scalars.

A morphism from the restricted finite right model is determined by its finite pure tensors: forget scalar actions, conjugate by integralScalarReductionIso, commute sectionwise inverse image with sheafification, and use the sheafification universal property and tensor-product induction.

Obtain the inverse finite formula by applying inverse to the given forward formula with middle coefficient one. Precompose the transition square by that inverse isomorphism. Apply the preceding pure-tensor extensionality and the two transition formulas, then the finite formula. The middle transition preserves one; naturality of the finite constant coefficient comparisons identifies the remaining scalar.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03EK and 03EL, tensor-product section and pullback lemma; T2 direct uniqueness calculation from the supplied normalized formulas, 2026-10-28.

statement_change.what: The original statement omitted CompletedFormula for b. Its five hypotheses do not mention b, so replacing b by its negative leaves them unchanged but reverses its composite in the claimed quotient square. For identity g and E=L over an odd prime, the normalized quotient of a free rank-one degree-zero complex is nonzero and differs from its negative. Add the normalization already present in the source argument and in the only caller scalar_finite_model; no target or parent theorem statement changes.
